title: Brokered phase-fission policy to balance latency and throughput for mixed prefill/decode workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current prefill/decode arbiter treats phase boundaries coarsely which causes oscillation between very low-latency but low-throughput prefill bursts and high-throughput decode windows that degrade tail latency for interactive customers. We also observe suboptimal kernel selection in mixed-phase batches (prefill+decode) because the scheduler groups requests by arrival time rather than phase composition, causing inefficient attention kernel paths and KV cache churn.

Goal: Implement a brokered phase-fission policy that: 1) splits work at sub-phase granularity based on configurable latency budgets and kernel compatibility; 2) routes sub-phases to optimized kernel-class lanes (e.g., short-seq attention, fused fast-attn, quantized decode path); 3) enforces fairness across customers and request classes so that low-latency interactive flows are protected while preserving throughput for batchy decodes.

Design summary: The policy introduces a light-weight broker layer that inspects each request's prefill/decode profile (tokens, context length, temperature, sync vs streaming) and assigns a "split score". High split-score requests are fragmented into shorter micro-phases which can run on low-latency fast-path kernels. Lower scores are colocated to throughput lanes where continuous batching is prioritized. The broker also maintains per-customer soft quotas and a proportional fairness token to avoid starvation.

Key components and interactions: 
- Split heuristic: weighted function of remaining decode tokens, CPU/GPU kernel affinity, KV cache hit probability, and end-to-end latency budget.
- Kernel tagging: runtime maintains tags for kernel families; broker uses tags to create homogeneous micro-batches to reduce kernel switching.
- Fairness token bucket: per-tenant reservoir replenished based on SLA tier and recent usage; tokens spent to gain latency-priority.
- Fallbacks: if a target kernel lane is congested, policy can 1) hedge by duplicating first token generation on both lanes for short penalty, or 2) fall back to compatible slower kernel with admission control.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Splitting increases scheduling overhead and KV cache fragmentation (cost). We mitigate with max-split-per-request and cache affinity heuristics.
- Hedging reduces latency tail but increases GPU work; use only for high split-score requests under SLO breach conditions.
- More aggressive kernel grouping improves throughput but can hurt fairness; balancing via proportional tokens and per-route weights.

Acceptance criteria: 
- 50th / 95th / 99th percentile latency for interactive benchmark improves by >=10% / 8% / 5% respectively at baseline load compared to current arbiter.
- Throughput for batch decode workloads degrades by <=5% at same cost profile.
- No tenant sees sustained starvation (defined as >5x increase in request latency or >30% reduction in qps for 5 minutes).

Observability: Add per-lane metrics: lane_throughput, lane_latency_p95, kernel_switches, kv_cache_miss_rate, split_rate, fairness_tokens_consumed. Surface in console per-route and per-tenant dashboards with compare-to-baseline.

Rollout plan: 
1) Unit tests for split heuristic, kernel tagging, and token bucket.
2) Local simulator (cycle 1) to validate latency/throughput trade-offs across synthetic mixes.
3) Canary into dedicated pool with opt-in routing for 5% of interactive traffic for a week. Monitor metrics and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% if stable.

Docs & artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/456789012/phase-fission-brokered-policy (draft).
Perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/244 (WIP).
Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298 (draft).

Next steps: finalize split weights after simulator runs, implement kernel tagging hooks in runtime kernel registry, and add observability counters.
